items.title: This new tool aims to identify and trace AI videos back to their source models
items.excerpt: A UC Riverside team built SAGA (Source Attribution of Generative AI Videos), one of the first large-scale frameworks to trace an AI-generated clip back to the model that made it by reading the distinctive visual 'fingerprints' each generator leaves behind - a provenance tool with direct implications for deepfakes, rights and AI disclosure in filmmaking.

items.title: NVIDIA tackles deepfakes and opens the door to AI agents at SIGGRAPH 2026
items.excerpt: At SIGGRAPH 2026 NVIDIA introduced a Synthetic Video Detector NIM microservice to help newsrooms and broadcasters flag AI-generated video, and showcased AI-agent integrations (via MCP) reaching into creative tools like Adobe and Unreal Engine - signalling how detection and agentic AI are entering the production and post pipeline.

items.title: Lightcraft launches beta for Spark Story interactive previz tool
items.excerpt: Lightcraft is opening a rolling beta of Spark Story, an interactive previz platform that pairs a 3D asset library (World Labs 'Marble' environments, 300+ assets), one-click real-time 24p/25p live-action compositing on iOS, and live global collaboration over scripts, Gaussian splats and USD assets - aimed at shaping shots and cutting costs from day one of preproduction.

items.title: SIGGRAPH: 'Kok Boru' director Amina Omirjan talks frankly about the making of Higgsfield AI's new short
items.excerpt: Higgsfield premiered 'Kok Boru,' a 15-minute historical-drama short, at SIGGRAPH 2026, and its director details the hybrid human-AI pipeline: hand-drawn character designs, props and painted textures define look and performance before 'conditioning' the AI output - a candid, craft-first look at where generative animation actually helps and where it doesn't.

items.title: AI YouTuber Gossip Goblin plans to release AI film 'Gods Don't Give Gifts' in movie theaters
items.excerpt: Variety reports on Gossip Goblin's plan to bring the AI-generated anthology 'Gods Don't Give Gifts' to theaters this fall - a marker of AI-native creators moving from viral YouTube shorts to theatrical features. (Same story as the Deadline item; kept for outlet diversity.)

items.title: Venice-set Reply AI Film Festival unveils finalists and jury
items.excerpt: The third Reply AI Film Festival, running alongside the Venice Film Festival, selected 10 AI-made shorts from 3,000 submissions across 76 countries and named a jury including Gabriele Salvatores, Catherine Hardwicke and Jed Weintrob. Winners across Best Short Film, an AI for Good Award and the Reply AI Studios Grand Prix are announced September 6.
